title: Effective Surface Passivation for Single-Molecule Studies of Chromatin and Topoisomerase II
author: Le, Gao, et al.
materials: The torsionally constrained (TC) 64-mer DNA template is formed by ligating two 500-bp multi-labeled adapters, one to each end, to a DNA template consisting of 64 tandem repeats of a 197 bp sequence, each repeat containing a 601-nucleosome positioning element (NPE)14 (Figure 1A). The 64-mer DNA is constructed by using a method similar to that previously described.15 The 500-bp adapter sequence is constructed by concatenating three 145-bp sequences that were found to have low affinity for nucleosomes16 to prevent additional nucleosomes from assembling on the adapters. The low nucleosome affinity sequence is flanked by a set of restriction sequences so that it can be employed in various constructs.1.Obtain the 64-mer DNA from P197NRL-64ex:a.To generate the P197NRL-64ex plasmid (a.k.a. pMDW108), transform the plasmid into NEB E. coli stable competent cells according to the manufacturer’s protocol. The protocol is found here: https://www.neb.com/en-us/protocols/2013/10/30/high-efficiency-transformation-protocol-c3040h.i.Plate the cells, grow colonies for 16–18 h at 30°C.ii.Select individual colonies into liquid growth media, and grow cultures for 16–18 h at 30°C.iii.Purify the plasmids using a Qiagen Qiaprep kit following the manufacturer’s instructions. The protocol is found here : https://www.qiagen.com/us/products/discovery-and-translational-research/dna-rna-purification/dna-purification/plasmid-dna/qiaprep-spin-miniprep-kit.iv.Check the concentration of the plasmid using a spectrophotometer.Note: Any common plasmid preparation kit or DNA purification kit (which will be mentioned in following sections) should work. For DNA purification, choose the kit that can handle > 10-kb DNA.CRITICAL: Care must be taken to minimize a change in NPE repeats. Keep the plasmid sample from each independent colony separate for size screening. The plasmid can lose or gain repeats during transformation, and thus, it is essential to check its size using the following procedure. For this reason, it is also advisable to store the plasmid in the form of purified DNA and not in the form of transformed cells.b.Digest each plasmid sample with BstXI and BglI.c.Run the resulting digestion on a 0.8% agarose gel. Run the gel at ∼100 V for 2 h to select the plasmid with the correct size (12,667 bp) and highest homogeneity (green arrows, Figure 1B). Do not select the samples with slightly shorter fragments (red arrows, Figure 1B), indicative of the loss of the 601 repeats.d.Pool the high-quality plasmid samples and double digest with BstXI and BglI. After preparing the surface-anchored nucleosome sample as will be described in Section F, the sample chamber is mounted onto an optical tweezers or a magnetic tweezers instrument. To obtain accurate extension measurements on magnetic tweezers and correct for instrument drift, it is essential to generate fiducial markers. In previous experiments, a small population of magnetic beads introduced during the tether anchoring step would nonspecifically get stuck on the surface and those stuck beads were employed as fiducial markers. However, the improved surface passivation of our described protocol effectively suppresses nonspecific bead sticking. Therefore, we needed to manually generate beads that are stuck on the surface that serve as fiduciary markers. To generate stable fiducial markers under our surface conditions, we developed a method using biotin-and-digoxygenin-labeled DNA to strongly anchor streptavidin-coated magnetic beads to an anti-digoxygenin-coated surface that could resist magnetic pulling under a few tens of piconewton forces.38.Make the double-labeled sticky DNA adapters (labeled with both biotin and digoxygenin) as described in “materials and equipment”39.Prepare the double-labeled 500-bp DNA-coated magnetic beads.a.In a 500-μL tube, add 0.35 μL of washed streptavidin-coated T1 magnetic beads into 99 μL PBS 1X. Mix and sonicate for 30 s. For optimal performance, wash the beads as described in the section wash the streptavidin-coated magnetic beads or streptavidin-coated cylinders.CRITICAL: It is critical to use the Dynabeads MyOne Streptavidin T1 magnetic beads when working with nucleosome fibers. We found that other streptavidin-coated magnetic beads, such as Dynabeads MyOne Streptavidin C1 from Thermo Fisher and S1420S from NEB, could induce histone loss, potentially due to the iron leakage from the bead core in a buffer containing EDTA.b.Cool the bead solution down by leaving the tube on ice for 40 s. Then add 2.5 μL of the 93-nM 500-bp biotin-dig-labeled adapter. Mix well and incubate at 4°C for 30 min.c.Pull down the magnetic beads by putting the tube in a magnet rack. Discard the supernatant and then add 50 μL PBS 1X and re-suspend the beads. Store this bead solution at 4°C.CRITICAL: It is critical to discard the supernatant with unbound sticky DNA adapters as it could be readily adsorbed to the surface and compete with DNA tethering during the DNA anchoring steps.40.Generate the stuck bead fiducial marker.a.Incubate a hydrophobic nitrocellulose-coated grease sample chamber with ∼50 μL of 1–20 ng/μL anti-digoxygenin for 30 min.b.Dilute 2.5 μL of the sticky DNA-bound bead solution, as prepared in the previous steps, into 65 μL of PBS 1X and mix well. Sonicate for 10 s.c.Flow the mixture into the sample chamber and incubate for 10 min at 20°C–23°C.d.Flush out the unbound beads by introducing 95 μL beta-casein 25 mg/mL (see “beta-casein preparation”) to start the surface passivation step.e.On a Magnetic Tweezers (MT), mount the sample chamber and check for stuck beads. Following the described protocol, there are typically ∼10 stuck beads per a 562 μm × 350 μm FOV. Quickly rotate the magnet to identify stably stuck beads (which stay fixed under magnetic rotation) and use these beads as references.Note: If there are too few or too many stuck beads, increase or decrease the amount of DNA-bound beads in the dilution in Step 3, respectively.

steps.title: Obtain 64‑mer plasmid
steps.instruction: Transform p197NRL‑64ex (pMDW108) into NEB stable E. coli, plate and grow colonies 16–18 h at 30 °C, inoculate liquid culture and grow 16–18 h at 30 °C, purify plasmid with Qiagen Qiaprep kit, measure concentration spectrophotometrically and keep each colony’s plasmid separate for size screening.

steps.title: Digest plasmid and select correct band
steps.instruction: Digest each plasmid sample with BstXI and BglI, run 0.8 % agarose gel at ~100 V for 2 h, select the ~12 667 bp band (green arrows) and avoid shorter fragments (red arrows).

steps.title: Large‑scale double digestion
steps.instruction: In a 230 µL reaction combine 3.5 µL ultrapure H₂O, 23 µL FastDigest Green Buffer 10× (1× final), ≤310 ng/µL (≈200 µL) P197NRL‑64ex (≈356 ng/µL, ≤310 ng/µL final), 1.5 µL FastDigest BstXI (≈1 µL/100 µL), 2.0 µL FastDigest BglI (≈1 µL/100 µL), bring to 230 µL with water, incubate 37 °C 1.5 h (check at 45 min on 0.8 % gel).

steps.title: Gel‑purify 64‑mer DNA
steps.instruction: Load the entire digested sample into a large well of a 10‑cm 0.8 % agarose gel, run 40 min at 90 V (increase voltage for longer gels to maintain ~9 V/cm), excise the top 12.7 kb band without UV exposure, elute DNA with Zymoclean Large Fragment Recovery kit per manufacturer’s instructions.

steps.title: Digest 500‑bp adapters
steps.instruction: Prepare biotin‑labeled and dig‑labeled 500‑bp adapters; for each, in a 120 µL reaction mix 6.0 µL water, 12.0 µL FastDigest Buffer 10×, 99.0 µL purified adapter (48 ng/µL for biotin, 26 ng/µL for dig), 4–5 µL BglI (biotin) or 2–3 µL BstXI (dig), incubate 37 °C 2.5 h; purify each with PureLink PCR columns using 10 mM Tris‑Cl pH 8.0 + 0.1 mM EDTA pre‑warmed to 50 °C, measure concentrations with NanoDrop and adjust elution volumes to equalize concentrations.

steps.title: Ligate adapters to 64‑mer DNA
steps.instruction: Set up a 120 µL ligation with 17.5 µL water, 12 µL T4 10× buffer (1×), 57 µL purified 64‑mer DNA (341 ng/µL, 40.8 nM), 19.5 µL biotin‑adapter (190 nM, 24.5 nM final), 15.5 µL dig‑adapter (190 nM, 24.5 nM final), 15.5 µL T4 ligase (400 U/µL, ~8 U/µL final), mix gently with a wide‑bore tip, keep on ice, incubate 16 °C 8–10 h, heat‑inactivate 65 °C 30 min, then purify with PureLink PCR columns and elute in 10 mM Tris‑Cl pH 8.0 + 1 mM EDTA; store at 4 °C.

steps.title: Prepare dialysis buffers
steps.instruction: Make high‑salt, low‑salt, and zero‑salt buffers as described in Materials and Equipment; add 1 M DTT to zero‑salt buffer before use; keep all buffers at 4 °C.

steps.title: Clean and autoclave glassware
steps.instruction: Rinse two 500‑mL beakers, one 2000‑mL beaker, and one 100‑mL graduated cylinder with ultrapure H₂O, wash gently with diluted soap, rinse again, then autoclave glassware, PCR‑tube caps and rims using the ‘Fast’ cycle for 30 min.

steps.title: Prepare dialysis membrane
steps.instruction: Cut a piece of 6–8 kD MWCO dialysis membrane, soak in ultrapure H₂O for ≥10 min, trim edges with clean scissors, open gently with tweezers without tearing.

steps.title: Thaw histone octamers
steps.instruction: Retrieve histone octamers from –80 °C, thaw at 4 °C or on ice, gently pipette up/down until no crystals remain.

steps.title: Mix DNA, histones, and competitor
steps.instruction: For each desired histone‑to‑DNA molar ratio (0.25:1, 0.5:1, 1:1, 2.5:1), in a 500‑µL tube on ice combine ultrapure H₂O, nucleosome assembly buffer 2× (3.34 µL, 4.68 µL, or 5.36 µL depending on ratio), 15 µL each of 2× buffer, 15 µL 64‑mer DNA (213 ng/µL, 22.73 nM), 5 µL each of 147‑bp competitor DNA (268 ng/µL), and the appropriate volume of histone octamers (2.7 µM stock: 2.69 µL, 1.35 µL, or 0.67 µL). Total volume 30 µL per mixture.

steps.title: Assemble dialysis chambers
steps.instruction: Place 500 µL high‑salt buffer onto the soaked membrane to soak, discard excess, then for each 30 µL mixture pipette onto a PCR‑tube cap, lay the membrane over the cap, cover with a PCR‑tube rim, and press down with a clean 1.5‑mL PCR tube to form a sealed chamber; keep caps spaced several centimeters apart and record conditions.

steps.title: Run continuous salt dialysis
steps.instruction: Attach membranes with chambers to a Slide‑A‑Lyzer floatation assembly, submerge in high‑salt buffer, connect pump tubing to low‑salt, high‑salt, and waste beakers; run pump at 1.2 mL/min for 18 h, then increase to 2.4 mL/min until low‑salt buffer is exhausted (~45 min), add 1 M DTT to zero‑salt buffer, transfer assembly into zero‑salt buffer, stir with magnetic bar for ≥4 h at 4 °C.

steps.title: Retrieve nucleosome arrays
steps.instruction: Remove membranes from zero‑salt buffer, pipette off all buffer from chambers, puncture each membrane with a pipette tip, collect the nucleosome solution into a 0.5‑mL tube, store at 4 °C (stable for months), and assess occupancy by gel or stretching assay.

steps.title: Assay nucleosome occupancy by gel
steps.instruction: For each assembly dilute 2 µL sample in 8 µL 10 mM Tris‑Cl pH 8.0, 1 mM EDTA, 5 % (v/v) glycerol, load onto a 10‑cm 0.7 % agarose gel, run at 15 V/cm in 0.2× TBE at 20‑23 °C for 30 min, post‑stain with ethidium bromide and evaluate band mobility and disappearance of competitor DNA.

steps.title: Prepare 1‑2 % nitrocellulose solution
steps.instruction: In a fume hood combine 4‑8 % collodion solution (Sigma Cat# 09986‑500 mM) with amyl acetate to a final volume of 10 mL yielding 1‑2 % nitrocellulose; invert tube a few times, cap tightly, store in amber bottle at 20‑23 °C up to 3 months.

steps.title: Clean glass slide and coverslip
steps.instruction: Clean a glass slide and coverslip as described in the cleaning protocol, dry completely under airflow, and place the slide in an empty tip box.

steps.title: Apply nitrocellulose coating
steps.instruction: Drop 70‑80 µL of the 1‑2 % nitrocellulose solution onto the slide, gently place a clean coverslip on top to spread the solution without large bubbles, then slide the coverslip off (do not lift) to leave a uniform nitrocellulose film on the coverslip; gently dry slide and coverslip under airflow.

steps.title: Ethanol harden nitrocellulose on coverslip
steps.instruction: Place the coated coverslip into a 50‑mL tube containing 95 % EtOH, incubate 20‑23 °C for 5 min (do not use 100 % EtOH), then decant EtOH and dry the coverslip in an oven at 80 °C for 10 min, cool to 20‑23 °C, rinse gently with ultrapure H₂O (twice, careful not to strip film), and dry with airflow.

steps.title: Assemble nitrocellulose flow chamber
steps.instruction: Using a blunt‑tip syringe pre‑filled with high‑vacuum grease, create two parallel grease walls on the nitrocellulose‑coated coverslip, place the cleaned slide on top, and press firmly to seal; keep the assembled chamber in a clean tip box for ≥24 h (preferably 48 h) at 20‑23 °C to allow grease diffusion and surface hydrophobicity.

steps.title: Prepare double‑labeled sticky DNA adapters
steps.instruction: Generate 500‑bp adapters bearing both biotin and digoxygenin as described in Materials and Equipment (same as step 5 but double‑labeled).

steps.title: Prepare DNA‑coated magnetic beads
steps.instruction: In a 500‑µL tube add 0.35 µL washed Dynabeads MyOne Streptavidin T1 to 99 µL PBS 1X, sonicate 30 s, place on ice 40 s, add 2.5 µL 93 nM biotin‑dig‑labeled 500‑bp adapter, incubate 4 °C 30 min, pull beads with magnet, discard supernatant, resuspend in 50 µL PBS 1X, store at 4 °C; discard supernatant containing unbound adapters.

steps.title: Generate stuck‑bead fiducial markers
steps.instruction: Incubate the nitrocellulose‑grease chamber with ~50 µL 1–20 ng/µL anti‑digoxygenin for 30 min, dilute 2.5 µL bead solution into 65 µL PBS 1X, sonicate 10 s, flow the mixture into the chamber, incubate 10 min at 20‑23 °C, then flush unbound beads with 95 µL beta‑casein 25 mg/mL to begin surface passivation; mount chamber on magnetic tweezers, rotate magnet to locate ~10 stably stuck beads per 562 µm × 350 µm field of view.

steps.title: Prepare beta‑casein solution (40 mL, 25 mg/mL)
steps.instruction: Add 400 µL 1 M Tris‑Cl pH 8.3 to a beta‑casein bottle, add 400 µL 5 M NaCl, then add 30 mL ultrapure H₂O, cap tightly and seal with parafilm, attach bottle to a vertical wheel with strong tape, spin at 20 % power 16–18 h at 4 °C, then incubate 2 h at 4 °C until bubbles disappear; aliquot into 1.5 mL tubes, store at –80 °C (long‑term) or thaw at 4 °C, pipette up/down 7×, centrifuge 5 s, aliquot into smaller tubes, store at –20 °C and use within 2 months.

steps.title: Prepare 20 mg/mL NaN₃ solution
steps.instruction: Dissolve 0.4 g NaN₃ in 20 mL ultrapure H₂O to obtain 20 mg/mL; mix in a 50 mL Falcon tube, invert a few times, cap tightly, store at 20‑23 °C up to 3 months; wear gloves and mask, prepare fresh on day of experiment.

steps.title: Prepare nucleosome assembly 2× buffer
steps.instruction: Combine 252 µL ultrapure H₂O, 40 mM Tris‑Cl pH 7.5, 8 µL 0.5 M EDTA (2 mM final), 8 µL 5 M NaCl (4 M final), 1.6 mL DTT 1 M (20 mM final), 20 µL acetylated BSA 20 mg/mL (0.2 mg/mL final), bring to 2000 µL total; store at –20 °C up to 1 year.

steps.title: Prepare chromatin dilution 10× buffer
steps.instruction: Mix 720 µL ultrapure H₂O, 30 mM Tris‑Cl pH 8.0, 250 µL KCl 2 M (500 mM final), bring to 1000 µL; make fresh on day of experiment.

steps.title: Prepare topoisomerase dilution buffer
steps.instruction: Combine 715.5 µL ultrapure H₂O, 0.5 mM TCEP (0.5 µL of 1 M stock), 0.1 mg/mL beta‑casein (4 µL of 25 mg/mL), bring to 1000 µL; store at –20 °C up to 2 months, add beta‑casein immediately before use.

steps.title: Prepare topoisomerase reaction buffer
steps.instruction: Mix 1760.6 µL ultrapure H₂O, 10 mM Tris‑Cl pH 8.0 (20 µL of 1 M), 50 mM NaCl (20 µL of 5 M), 50 mM KCl (20 µL of 2 M), 3 mM MgCl₂ (6 µL of 1 M), 0.4 mM EDTA (0.1 µL of 500 mM), 1 mM ATP (20 µL of 100 mM), 1 mM DTT (2 µL of 1 M), 0.5 mM TCEP (1 µL of 1 M), 1.5 mg/mL beta‑casein (120 µL of 25 mg/mL); bring to 2000 µL total, keep on ice, make fresh on day of experiment.

steps.title: Prepare topoisomerase flushing buffer
steps.instruction: Mix 1782.6 µL ultrapure H₂O, 10 mM Tris‑Cl pH 8.0 (20 µL of 1 M), 50 mM NaCl (20 µL of 5 M), 50 mM KCl (20 µL of 2 M), 2 mM MgCl₂ (4 µL of 1 M), 0.4 mM EDTA (0.1 µL of 500 mM), 1 mM DTT (2 µL of 1 M), 0.5 mM TCEP (1 µL of 1 M), 1.5 mg/mL beta‑casein (120 µL of 25 mg/mL); bring to 2000 µL total, make fresh on day of experiment, keep on ice.
